result.title: Trainspotting: Learning Object-Centric 3D Reconstruction from Found Photos
result.summary: State-of-the-art feedforward reconstruction models perform poorly on in-the-wild object-centric photo collections. They are trained largely on single-session object captures whose images vary in viewpoint while the object and its environment remain nearly fixed. Public photo archives contain a different form of multi-view data. They hold found photos of the same object or design: photos taken independently by many people across years, environments, cameras, and sometimes physical units. In this work, we introduce Trainspotting, a dataset of 12,068 objects and 311,886 photos from Wikimedia Commons. We reconstruct each object to recover camera poses, multi-view stereo depth, and object masks. We categorize the objects into three regimes: objects fixed at one site, objects that move between sites, and designs shared by many physical units. Evaluating recent feedforward reconstruction models on Trainspotting shows that they fail most severely in the last two regimes. Fine-tuning VGGT-$Ω$ on Trainspotting significantly improves camera pose, depth, and 3D geometry on held-out objects. We observe similar improvements on the independent NAVI in-the-wild benchmark, which contains photos of each object in different environments. Performance on conventional benchmarks remains largely unchanged.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作构建了来自 Wikimedia Commons 的「found photos」数据集（12,068 个物体、311,886 张跨年份与环境拍摄的照片），并用于评测与微调前馈式三维重建模型在相机位姿、深度与几何上的表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文核心是三维重建数据与基准，评价指标为位姿、深度和几何精度，不涉及 latent 推理状态、证据使用或停止决策等主线问题，也未见可供核查的 latent 视觉状态或推理机制线索。
